title: Vectors: Components, Magnitude and Direction
seo_title: Vectors Worksheet: Component Form, Magnitude and Direction | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on vectors: component form, magnitude, direction angle, components from magnitude and direction, and velocity and force problems. 100 questions.
key_big: A vector = magnitude + direction. Component form is terminal minus initial.
key_sub: Magnitude √(a² + b²); components ⟨r cos θ, r sin θ⟩.
body_html:
How it works

  • A vector has magnitude (length) and direction. From P(x1, y1) to Q(x2, y2): v = ⟨x2 − x1, y2 − y1⟩ (terminal minus initial).
  • Magnitude: ‖⟨a, b⟩‖ = √(a² + b²).
  • Direction angle: the reference angle is tan⁻¹|b/a|; then choose the quadrant from the signs of a and b.
  • From magnitude r and direction θ: v = ⟨r cos θ, r sin θ⟩.
Example

Find the vector from P(2, −1) to Q(−4, 7) and its magnitude.

⟨−4 − 2, 7 − (−1)⟩ = ⟨−6, 8⟩

√(36 + 64) = 10

Answer: ⟨−6, 8⟩, magnitude 10

Example

Find the direction angle of ⟨−3, 3⟩.

Reference angle tan⁻¹(1) = 45°

Quadrant II

Answer: 135°

Common mistakes

  • Subtracting initial minus terminal. Always terminal minus initial.
  • Adding the components to get the magnitude. Use the Pythagorean theorem.
  • Using tan⁻¹(b/a) without checking the quadrant.
  • Swapping cosine and sine: the x-component uses cos θ.

faq.q: How do you find the component form of a vector?
faq.a: Subtract the coordinates of the initial point from the coordinates of the terminal point: ⟨x₂ − x₁, y₂ − y₁⟩.

faq.q: How do you find the magnitude of a vector?
faq.a: Use the Pythagorean theorem: the magnitude of ⟨a, b⟩ is √(a² + b²).

faq.q: How do you find the direction angle?
faq.a: Find the reference angle with tan⁻¹|b/a|, then adjust for the quadrant the vector points into.

faq.q: How do you write a vector from its magnitude and direction?
faq.a: Multiply the magnitude by cos θ for the x-component and by sin θ for the y-component.

items.q: A plane flies due north at 200 mph, and the wind blows due east at 40 mph. To the nearest mph, what is the plane's ground speed?
items.e: The velocities are ⟨40, 200⟩ together, so the speed is √(40² + 200²) ≈ 204 mph.
